assignments.brief_reason: Focuses on general content cues (language/tone) without clearly matching the specific threat/toxicity or fairness/mirror-pair standard themes.
Rejects rhetoric/profanity while seeking substance for healthy conversation, aligning with removing vulgar/toxic material.
Emphasizes distancing from feelings and allowing equal time, consistent with applying a consistent moderation standard across sides.
Accepts speech broadly but removes/concerns arise only when inciting/encouraging violence (with related constraints).
Removal based on fact-claims and blaming politicians/policies is not clearly threat/toxicity or violence-exception content.
Speech is protected except for illegal/harm/violence-related content.
Avoids harmful/rude content, which fits the ‘remove for threats and toxicity’ moderation bar.
Describes a gut-first heuristic without mapping to any specific moderation rule theme.
Personal preference ('want to see it') for keep vs remove does not fit the codebook themes.
Frames decisions as ethical-values wording, which doesn’t clearly correspond to the defined threat/toxicity or violence-exception rules.
Treats explicit language/manipulation as disqualifying; closest to removing content that becomes toxic or unacceptable.
Uses contrast between original vs mirror focus/wording, aligning with applying consistent comparison criteria across sides.
Relies on partisan trust/distrust to interpret mirrored content, which is not a moderation-standard theme.
Explicitly rejects based on negativity and cuss words (toxicity/vulgarity cue removal).
Removes based on mirror effect plus a foul-language rule, matching toxicity/vulgarity removal.
Keep most viewpoints and remove only when crossing a clear line, framed as free-speech boundary exceptions.
Says nothing seemed worth removing; this is more overall stance than a specific rule consistent with the themes.
Concrete standard: no personal attacks/bad language while restricting harassment/toxic content.
Removes for misinformation plus rudeness/mean-spiritedness and all-caps—explicit toxicity/uncivility cues.
Removes ad-hoc/emotionally phrased attacks, corresponding to toxicity/unacceptable attack content removal.
